title: Diagrams that change, with React Flow
description: Adds flow fences: a Mermaid flowchart drawn in the browser by React Flow and laid out by dagre, whose versions, split by lines of ---, are steps. Edges turn at right angles in lanes between the ranks, edges into one node sharing a trunk, unless edges= after the language, or edges: in the frontmatter, asks for step, bezier or straight ones. Nodes that stay glide to their new places while the edges keep square corners, new ones fade in, removed ones stay as ghosts for the step, and badges mark what is new, changed, moved or removed, except a node that only turns muted, which is just dimmed. Along the flow nodes keep their place as a diagram grows, unless anchor=center grows it from its middle, a node alone starting there. The diagram fits the room its slide leaves and reports a shrink below its drawn size like a Mermaid diagram; the README, the writing-slides skill and a VS Code snippet document it.

context_before: A `mermaid` fence in the deck becomes an SVG when it builds, so load `mermaid-diagrams` for the syntax and its readability rules. Its rule against diagrams in files of their own is written for GitHub; here the fence goes in `slides.mdx` like any other. On a 16:9 slide keep to about six nodes, prefer `flowchart LR`, and keep labels to a word or two: the build warns when a diagram is too wide, and the check warns when its labels end up under 18 px.

added: A `flow` fence is a Mermaid flowchart drawn in the browser by [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev) and laid out by [dagre](https://github.com/dagrejs/dagre), for a diagram that changes while you talk. Lines of `---` split it into versions, and each version is a step: nodes that stay move to their new places, new ones fade in, and what a version removes stays as a dashed ghost until the next, so the printed slide shows the whole change.

Only the first version needs the `flowchart` line; later ones keep its direction. A node is the same node in every version that uses its id. Shapes, edge labels and `-->`, `-.->`, `==>` and `---` edges are Mermaid's, and a class gives a node a tone: `:::primary`, `:::muted`, `:::success`, `:::warning` or `:::danger`. After the language, `direction=TB` sets the direction and `duration=800` how long each change takes, in milliseconds; a second by default.

`edges=` after the language sets how edges are drawn. The default, `smoothstep`, runs them at right angles with rounded corners: an edge leaves the middle of its node's downstream side, turns in a lane between two ranks and goes around the nodes it skips, and edges into one node share a trunk. `step` keeps the corners square, `bezier` draws curves and `straight` straight lines. `edges: step` in the frontmatter sets the deck's default; a fence's `edges=` still wins. Mermaid's edge ids (`a e1@--> b`) and their `e1@{ … }` lines are dropped with a warning, since `edges=` shapes every edge of a fence.

`anchor=center` after the language grows a diagram from its middle: every version is centred along the flow too, so a node alone starts in the middle and moves aside as later versions add nodes around it, as when one table splits into several. By default each version keeps its nodes where the layout puts them along the flow, so a version that adds a rank leaves the rest in place.
A node a version changes carries a badge, and new edges draw in green:
| New     | is not in the version before                                    |
| Changed | has a new label, shape or tone; turning `:::muted` only dims it |
| Moved   | no longer comes from a node that is still there                 |
| Removed | is gone, and stays as a ghost for this step                     |

The diagram fills the room its slide leaves, up to 1.25 times its size, and shrinks when the room is smaller; the slide's corner says so, since its labels then fall under 18 px. Five nodes fit in a row, and four ranks top to bottom. In VS Code, typing `flow` in a slide offers a fence to start from.
## A `flow` fence animates a diagram from one version to the next
Lines of `---` split the fence into versions, and each is a step. Redis is
new, Postgres moved behind it, and the search index is gone: a removed node
stays as a ghost, so the printed slide shows the whole change. React Flow
draws the diagram and dagre lays it out. Edges turn at right angles in lanes
between the ranks; `edges=bezier` after the language draws curves instead.

content: The `flow` fence of this deck: when to use it over `mermaid`, its syntax, how its edges are drawn, what its badges mean, and how much fits.

A `mermaid` fence is drawn once, when the deck builds, and suits a diagram that stays the same. A `flow` fence is drawn in the browser by React Flow, so it can change as the talk goes: use it when the change is the point, such as an architecture before and after a migration, a request path that gains a cache, or a pipeline that loses a stage. The versions go in one fence on one slide, never in a diagram per slide.
A Mermaid flowchart, with a line of `---` between versions. Each version is a step, animated from the one before, and the print view shows the last.
## A cache in front of Postgres took the search index's place
- Only the first version needs `flowchart LR`; later ones keep its direction.
- A node is the same node in every version that uses its id, so `db` above moves where a new id would fade in as a new node. Changing its label keeps the node and marks it Changed.
- Shapes are Mermaid's: `[box]`, `(rounded)`, `([stadium])`, `((circle))`, `{diamond}`, `{{hexagon}}`, `[(cylinder)]` and `[[subroutine]]`. Others are drawn as boxes, with a warning.

- Edges are `-->`, `-.->` (dotted), `==>` (thick), `---` (no arrow) and `-->|label|`, one edge per pair of nodes. Subgraphs are drawn without their frame. Mermaid's edge ids (`a e1@--> b`) and their `e1@{ … }` lines are dropped with a warning: `edges=` shapes every edge of a fence.
- `:::primary`, `:::muted`, `:::success`, `:::warning` or `:::danger` after a node gives it a tone. `style` and `classDef` are ignored.

- After the language: `direction=TB` (or `LR`, `RL`, `BT`), `duration=800`, how long each change takes in milliseconds, a second by default, and `edges=step` (or `smoothstep`, `bezier`, `straight`), how edges are drawn.

- `anchor=center` after the language centres every version along the flow too, so the diagram grows from its middle: a node alone starts there and moves aside as the next version adds nodes around it, as when one table splits into several. Leave it out for a chain that gains a stage: by default nodes keep their place along the flow, and only those past the new rank move.
| `smoothstep` | Right angles with rounded corners; the default | Almost everything: architecture, request paths, lineage |
| `step` | Right angles with square corners | A schematic look: pipelines, networks, a deck that already has hard edges |
| `bezier` | Curves | A few nodes with few crossings, where a softer look matters more than tidy lines |
| `straight` | A straight line from node to node | Small diagrams where every edge joins neighbouring ranks; a line that skips a rank can cross the nodes in between |

Right-angle edges leave the middle of a node's downstream side and reach the middle of the next one's upstream side, turning in lanes between the ranks. Edges into one node share a trunk, every other edge gets a lane of its own, ordered to cross as few lines as it can, and an edge that skips a rank goes around the nodes in it. A label sits on its edge where it reads, never on a node. An edge back against the flow goes round the outside of the diagram. When a version changes, the corners move and the lines stay straight.
`edges: step` in the frontmatter sets the deck's default, and a fence's `edges=` still wins. Pick one for the deck and keep to it; mix only to make a point.
Each version is compared with the one before, node by node, and a node that changed carries a badge:
| New | was not in the version before |
| Changed | has a new label, shape or tone, unless it only turns `:::muted`: dimming a node sets it aside without a badge |
| Moved | no longer comes from a node that is still there |
| Removed | is gone, and stays as a dashed ghost for this step |

New edges are green and removed ones dashed red. Plan the versions so each step changes what the speaker is talking about at that moment: a step that lights up four badges is a slide the audience reads instead of listening. A node that only gains an input is not marked; its new edge shows the change.

Measured on this deck at full size, with labels at 18 px, and the same for every `edges=`: a fan-in turns in one lane, and a gap only widens when more edges turn in it than it has lanes for, as after a node with four or more outputs.
| Diagram | Fits at full size | One more |
| Left to right | 5 nodes in a row | 6 shrink to 92% |
| Top to bottom | 4 ranks, under a one- or two-line headline | 5 shrink to 88% or 78% |
| Several nodes into one | 4 stacked, under a two-line headline | 5 shrink to 88% |

A diagram smaller than its room grows, up to 1.25 times. Past these limits it shrinks, and `pnpm check` warns that the slide was shrunk to fit: treat that as a failure, and cut nodes, shorten labels, or split the change across two slides.
